# Safe Administration of Medicines Policy

Document family: `family.medication.administration`
Version: 2.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Purpose and scope

This policy applies to all Alderbridge services and establishes the minimum
controls for receiving, preparing, administering and recording medicines. It
does not replace a person's prescription, care plan or PRN protocol. Staff must
work within their assessed competence and seek clinical advice whenever the
record, label and current instructions do not agree.

## Authorisation to administer

Only staff with current medicines training and a recorded competency assessment
may administer medicines without direct supervision. Agency staff must also
complete the local medicines orientation before their first medicines round.
The shift leader checks the allocation at the start of every shift.

## Seven checks

Immediately before administration, the member of staff must confirm the right person, medicine, dose, route, time, reason and documentation.
Identity must be
checked against the MAR and the person's agreed identifier; room number alone
is not an identifier. The medicine label must be legible, in date and consistent
with the current MAR instruction.

## Recording administration

The member of staff must sign the Medication Administration Record (MAR) immediately after observing that the person has taken the dose.
Staff must not pre-sign a MAR.
If the medicine is not given, the correct exception code and a contemporaneous note are required.

| Circumstance | MAR code | Immediate action |
|---|---|---|
| Person refuses | R | Record the reason offered and follow the care-plan escalation |
| Medicine unavailable | U | Inform the shift leader and arrange an urgent supply check |
| Clinical instruction to omit | O | Record the prescriber's name and instruction |
| Person away from service | A | Confirm the absence in the daily record |

## Missed, delayed or refused doses

Staff must not give a delayed dose until they have checked the medicine-specific
window or obtained clinical advice. A refused dose must be handled without
coercion. The shift leader must be informed before the end of the medicines
round, and urgent clinical advice is required where the medicine is time
critical or the care plan identifies a material risk.

## PRN medicines

PRN means medicine given when required. Before a PRN dose, staff must consult
the current protocol for indication, minimum interval and maximum daily dose.
The reason for administration and the observed outcome must be recorded. A PRN
medicine must not be offered merely because it appears on the MAR.

## Storage checks

Before administering a refrigerated medicine, staff must confirm that the
latest temperature record is within 2°C to 8°C.
If it is outside that range, the medicine must be quarantined and the medicines storage procedure followed; staff must not decide independently that the medicine remains usable.

## Controlled drugs

Where the controlled-drugs procedure requires a witness, both staff members
must complete the register at the time of administration. A later countersignature
does not satisfy the witness requirement.

## Incident escalation and audit

An unexplained MAR gap, incorrect dose, wrong person, wrong medicine or omitted
time-critical dose is a medication incident. Staff must first protect the person,
obtain clinical advice where needed, inform the shift leader and complete the
medication incident record. The registered manager arranges a monthly audit of
MAR records, stock balances and recurring exception codes.

## Preparation and interruption control

The administering worker prepares medicines for one person at a time and keeps the MAR available throughout the round. Medicines are not pre-poured for several people to save time. If preparation is interrupted before identity or medicine checks are complete, the worker returns to the beginning of the checking sequence.

Insulin, anticoagulants, controlled drugs and other locally identified high-risk medicines receive the additional checks stated in their protocol. Additional checks complement rather than replace the ordinary rights of administration. A witness does not transfer accountability away from the administering worker.

## Changes and reconciliation

A medicine change is accepted only from an authorised prescriber or through the approved clinical communication route. Handwritten MAR amendments identify the medicine, instruction, source, date, time and staff member, with a second check where the procedure requires one. Staff do not alter a MAR from an ambiguous voicemail or a relative's recollection.

After hospital attendance, admission, discharge or another care transition, the receiving worker reconciles the prescription, discharge information, supplied medicines and current MAR. Differences are clarified before the next affected dose unless a clinician gives an explicit safe interim direction.

## Monitoring and escalation

Where a prescription or care plan requires observations, the worker confirms the current result before administration and records it in the designated place. A result copied from an earlier shift is not a current observation. Values outside the stated parameters are escalated before the medicine is given.

Suspected adverse effects are responded to according to urgency. Staff seek emergency help for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or another life-threatening reaction, then follow internal reporting. Less urgent concerns are reported promptly to the prescriber or clinical service and documented with onset, observations and action taken.

## End-of-round reconciliation

At the end of the round, the administering worker checks that every due MAR entry has an administration code, a documented reason for omission or an active escalation. Unexplained blank boxes are resolved before handover. The trolley, refrigerator and controlled-drug storage are secured, and any stock discrepancy is escalated under the relevant procedure.

Audit identifies learning, repeated omissions, late administration, unclear records and unsafe workarounds. It is not used to replace real-time supervision or to add retrospective signatures to incomplete records.

An authorised staff member and an independent authorised witness must observe each controlled-drug administration. Both sign the register at the time of administration; a later countersignature is prohibited. The running balance is checked against physical stock after every entry.

A discrepancy must be escalated immediately, not at the end of the shift. The shift leader secures the cabinet, repeats the balance with a second witness and informs the registered manager. Where diversion or harm is suspected, safeguarding and incident-reporting procedures also apply.

Returned or expired controlled drugs are stored in the designated segregated section until pharmacy collection. Destruction requires the authorised witness and a contemporaneous register entry.

# Covert Administration of Medicines Policy

Document family: `family.medication.covert`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 August 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Covert administration means disguising medicine in food or drink without the person's knowledge. It is never justified merely because a person refuses medicine. A decision requires a decision-specific assessment that the person lacks capacity, a recorded best-interests process, prescriber agreement and pharmacy advice confirming the proposed method will not alter the medicine unsafely.

The plan must name each medicine, method, review date and circumstances requiring reconsideration. Staff follow the current authorised plan exactly and record every administration on the MAR. If the person regains capacity, the covert plan cannot continue on the authority of an earlier assessment.

# PRN Medicines Protocol

Document family: `family.medication.prn`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

PRN means medicine prescribed to be given when required. Before offering a PRN medicine, staff must check the person's current protocol for the indication, minimum interval, maximum dose in 24 hours and non-medicine measures to try first. A PRN entry on the MAR is not, by itself, enough information to administer safely.

Staff record the reason for the dose, time, quantity and observed outcome. If the medicine is ineffective, requested unusually often or refused when symptoms remain concerning, the shift leader must review the care plan and obtain clinical advice. PRN medicine must never be used for staff convenience or as an unrecorded response to distress.

The administering worker prepares medicines for one person at a time and keeps the MAR available throughout the round. Medicines are not pre-poured for several people to save time. If preparation is interrupted before identity or medicine checks are complete, the worker returns to the beginning of the checking sequence.

The medicine trolley remains locked whenever the authorised worker is not in direct control of it. Keys are carried by the designated worker and are not left in a drawer, door or shared hiding place. Medicines taken away from the normal administration area remain labelled and under the worker's control until administered or returned to secure storage.

## Omissions, refusal and swallowing difficulty

When a person refuses a medicine, staff respect the decision, record the refusal using the correct MAR code and consider any immediate clinical risk. They do not disguise the medicine in food or drink unless the covert-administration process has been lawfully completed for that specific medicine.

A medicine is not recorded as administered until staff have reasonable evidence it was taken. If a tablet is dropped, spat out or later found, staff preserve what is safe to preserve, record the facts and seek advice before offering a replacement dose. Uncertainty is escalated; it is not resolved by guessing that the dose was or was not absorbed.

New swallowing difficulty triggers clinical review. Staff do not crush tablets, open capsules or mix medicines with food unless current medicine-specific advice authorises that route. A general statement that the person “prefers medicines crushed” is not sufficient.

## Time-critical and high-risk medicines

The care plan identifies time-critical medicines and the permitted administration window. Staff prioritise these medicines when a round is disrupted and seek clinical advice if the window is likely to be missed. The standard two-hour round does not silently redefine a narrower prescribed interval.

Insulin, anticoagulants, controlled drugs and other locally identified high-risk medicines receive the additional checks stated in their protocol. ## Arrival and identity

All visitors must sign in at reception and wear the issued visitor badge.
A contractor must additionally show photographic identification and be met by the

Reception staff tell visitors how to recognise the fire alarm and direct them to
the assembly arrangement for that location.
Visitors must not use lifts during an evacuation and must remain with their host or follow staff instructions.

Visitors must not photograph records, staff or people supported without explicit

## Immediate protection

If anyone is in immediate danger, staff must call the emergency services and
take proportionate steps to reduce further harm. Evidence must be preserved;
staff should not confront an alleged perpetrator or conduct their own interview.

## Reporting

Every safeguarding concern must be reported to the shift leader or registered manager immediately and recorded before the staff member finishes the shift.
The registered manager decides whether to notify the local authority safeguarding
team, but a manager's absence must never delay immediate protective action.

## Speaking up

Staff may report directly to the safeguarding lead when the concern involves
their manager. No employee will be disadvantaged for raising a genuine concern
in good faith.

A risk-assessed supervised start may be authorised only by the Director of People where the DBS update-service status is confirmed and all other checks are complete. A pending first-time DBS application does not permit unsupervised work.

# COSHH Assessment Procedure

Document family: `family.health-safety.coshh`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Before a hazardous substance is introduced, the manager obtains the current safety data sheet and completes a COSHH assessment covering exposure routes, storage, handling, PPE, spill response and disposal. Manufacturer instructions are evidence, not a substitute for the workplace assessment.

Assessments are reviewed annually and immediately after a formulation, task or control changes. Decanted products must retain an identifiable label; drink containers must never be used.

Staff preserve potentially relevant records and continue ordinary lawful work unless the Privacy Team gives a specific restriction.

Identity is verified proportionately. Excessive identification can itself create risk. Information about other people is reviewed before disclosure, but the presence of third-party material does not justify rejecting an entire request without analysis.

## New systems and changes

A data protection impact assessment begins before high-risk processing is approved, procured or piloted. Triggers include systematic monitoring, new uses of sensitive data, large-scale matching, automated decisions with significant effects and technology that people would not reasonably expect.

Contracts with processors define instructions, confidentiality, security, assistance with rights and incidents, deletion or return, audit information and control of sub-processors. Procurement completion does not by itself approve a new purpose for existing care or workforce data.

## Incident containment

After reporting, staff take safe reversible containment such as recalling a message, asking a known unintended recipient to preserve and delete it, or disconnecting a lost logged-in device through IT. They do not remotely erase evidence, contact unknown recipients repeatedly, promise a particular regulatory outcome or access accounts outside their authority.

The Privacy Team coordinates risk assessment with operational, safeguarding, clinical and security colleagues. Decisions record the people affected, data sensitivity, likely consequences, containment, notification reasoning and further prevention work.

Employees should normally raise a grievance in writing with their line manager. If the grievance concerns that manager, it must be sent to the next manager or People Team.

An investigatory meeting establishes facts and is not itself a disciplinary hearing. The employee must receive the allegation, evidence and possible consequences in writing before a formal hearing.

Suspension is a neutral precaution, not a disciplinary sanction, and must be reviewed every ten working days. Employees may be accompanied at a formal hearing by a trade union representative or workplace colleague.

The registered manager takes immediate protective action, preserves evidence and informs the safeguarding lead without waiting for an employment decision. The employee must not investigate, approach witnesses or access records beyond what their current duties require.

HR must be informed immediately rather than within one working day. A documented multi-agency strategy determines whether internal fact-finding can begin. Suspension remains a neutral risk-control option, not an automatic response or finding of fault.

## Sharing and communication

Before sharing personal information, staff confirm the recipient, purpose, minimum necessary content and secure channel. Email address auto-complete must be checked before sending. Large distributions use an approved mailing tool or blind-copy arrangement where recipients should not see one another.

Telephone callers are verified using proportionate questions that do not disclose the answer. Staff do not confirm that a person receives care merely because the caller knows a name or address. Where urgent information is necessary to prevent serious harm, staff share the minimum needed and document the reason rather than delaying solely because routine consent cannot be obtained.

Personal information is not copied into consumer messaging, personal email, removable media or unapproved AI services. Photographs taken for care or incident purposes use an approved device and system; copies are removed from the capture device after successful secure transfer.

## Accuracy, minimisation and retention

Records distinguish observed fact, professional judgement and information supplied by another person. Material errors are corrected promptly without concealing the audit history. A disputed opinion is not rewritten as fact; the challenge and outcome are recorded through the appropriate process.

Forms and reports collect only fields needed for their stated purpose. Reusing existing information is preferable to repeatedly asking a person for the same sensitive details, provided the reuse is compatible and accurate. Free-text fields must not become a place to store unrelated allegations, passwords or copied identity documents.

The records retention schedule defines routine deletion periods. A legal hold, safeguarding need or active complaint may suspend deletion for identified records. Staff must not keep private “just in case” copies when the authoritative record has reached disposal.

## Data rights

A request to access, correct, restrict or object to use of personal information is forwarded to the Privacy Team on the day received. No special wording is required. Staff preserve potentially relevant records and continue ordinary lawful work unless the Privacy Team gives a specific restriction.

Identity is verified proportionately. Excessive identification can itself create risk. Information about other people is reviewed before disclosure, but the presence of third-party material does not justify rejecting an entire request without analysis.

Less urgent concerns are reported promptly to the prescriber or clinical service and documented with onset, observations and action taken.

At the end of the round, the administering worker checks that every due MAR entry has an administration code, a documented reason for omission or an active escalation. Employees submit requests through the rota system and should not make non-refundable arrangements until approval is recorded. A manager who cannot approve the requested dates discusses practical alternatives. Refusal must identify the operational reason; “service need” without an explanation is not sufficient. Employees remain responsible for submitting requests; a review reminder is not automatic approval.

## Sharing and communication

Before sharing personal information, staff confirm the recipient, purpose, minimum necessary content and secure channel. Email address auto-complete must be checked before sending. Large distributions use an approved mailing tool or blind-copy arrangement where recipients should not see one another.

Telephone callers are verified using proportionate questions that do not disclose the answer. Staff do not confirm that a person receives care merely because the caller knows a name or address. Where urgent information is necessary to prevent serious harm, staff share the minimum needed and document the reason rather than delaying solely because routine consent cannot be obtained.

Personal information is not copied into consumer messaging, personal email, removable media or unapproved AI services. Photographs taken for care or incident purposes use an approved device and system; copies are removed from the capture device after successful secure transfer.

## Accuracy, minimisation and retention

Records distinguish observed fact, professional judgement and information supplied by another person. Material errors are corrected promptly without concealing the audit history. A disputed opinion is not rewritten as fact; the challenge and outcome are recorded through the appropriate process.

Forms and reports collect only fields needed for their stated purpose. Reusing existing information is preferable to repeatedly asking a person for the same sensitive details, provided the reuse is compatible and accurate. Free-text fields must not become a place to store unrelated allegations, passwords or copied identity documents.

The records retention schedule defines routine deletion periods. A legal hold, safeguarding need or active complaint may suspend deletion for identified records. Staff must not keep private “just in case” copies when the authoritative record has reached disposal.

## Data rights

A request to access, correct, restrict or object to use of personal information is forwarded to the Privacy Team on the day received. No special wording is required. Staff preserve potentially relevant records and continue ordinary lawful work unless the Privacy Team gives a specific restriction.

Identity is verified proportionately. Excessive identification can itself create risk. Information about other people is reviewed before disclosure, but the presence of third-party material does not justify rejecting an entire request without analysis.

A person raising a genuine concern in good faith will not be disadvantaged, even when an investigation does not substantiate it. Deliberately false allegations are addressed separately and must not be assumed merely because evidence is incomplete.

## Purpose and scope

This policy applies to all Alderbridge services and establishes the minimum
controls for receiving, preparing, administering and recording medicines. It
does not replace a person's prescription, care plan or PRN protocol. Staff must
work within their assessed competence and seek clinical advice whenever the
record, label and current instructions do not agree.

## Authorisation to administer

Only staff with current medicines training and a recorded competency assessment
may administer medicines without direct supervision. Agency staff must also
complete the local medicines orientation before their first medicines round.
The shift leader checks the allocation at the start of every shift.

## Seven checks

Immediately before administration, the member of staff must confirm the right person, medicine, dose, route, time, reason and documentation.
Identity must be
checked against the MAR and the person's agreed identifier; room number alone
is not an identifier. The medicine label must be legible, in date and consistent
with the current MAR instruction.

## Recording administration

The member of staff must sign the Medication Administration Record (MAR) immediately after observing that the person has taken the dose.
Staff must not pre-sign a MAR.
If the medicine is not given, the correct exception code and a contemporaneous note are required.

| Medicine unavailable | U | Inform the shift leader and arrange an urgent supply check |
| Clinical instruction to omit | O | Record the prescriber's name and instruction |

## Changes and reconciliation

A medicine change is accepted only from an authorised prescriber or through the approved clinical communication route. Handwritten MAR amendments identify the medicine, instruction, source, date, time and staff member, with a second check where the procedure requires one. Staff do not alter a MAR from an ambiguous voicemail or a relative's recollection.

After hospital attendance, admission, discharge or another care transition, the receiving worker reconciles the prescription, discharge information, supplied medicines and current MAR. Differences are clarified before the next affected dose unless a clinician gives an explicit safe interim direction.

## Monitoring and escalation

Where a prescription or care plan requires observations, the worker confirms the current result before administration and records it in the designated place. A result copied from an earlier shift is not a current observation. Values outside the stated parameters are escalated before the medicine is given.

Suspected adverse effects are responded to according to urgency. Staff seek emergency help for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or another life-threatening reaction, then follow internal reporting. Less urgent concerns are reported promptly to the prescriber or clinical service and documented with onset, observations and action taken.

## End-of-round reconciliation

At the end of the round, the administering worker checks that every due MAR entry has an administration code, a documented reason for omission or an active escalation. Unexplained blank boxes are resolved before handover. The trolley, refrigerator and controlled-drug storage are secured, and any stock discrepancy is escalated under the relevant procedure.

Audit identifies learning, repeated omissions, late administration, unclear records and unsafe workarounds. It is not used to replace real-time supervision or to add retrospective signatures to incomplete records.

## Missed, delayed or refused doses

Staff must not give a delayed dose until they have checked the medicine-specific

coercion. The shift leader must be informed before the end of the medicines

PRN means medicine given when required. Before a PRN dose, staff must consult
the current protocol for indication, minimum interval and maximum daily dose.
The reason for administration and the observed outcome must be recorded. A PRN
medicine must not be offered merely because it appears on the MAR.

## Storage checks

Before administering a refrigerated medicine, staff must confirm that the
latest temperature record is within 2°C to 8°C.
If it is outside that range, the medicine must be quarantined and the medicines storage procedure followed; staff must not decide independently that the medicine remains usable.

## Controlled drugs

Where the controlled-drugs procedure requires a witness, both staff members
must complete the register at the time of administration. A later countersignature
does not satisfy the witness requirement.

## Incident escalation and audit

An unexplained MAR gap, incorrect dose, wrong person, wrong medicine or omitted

MAR records, stock balances and recurring exception codes.

The administering worker prepares medicines for one person at a time and keeps the MAR available throughout the round. Medicines are not pre-poured for several people to save time. # Covert Administration of Medicines Policy

Covert administration means disguising medicine in food or drink without the person's knowledge. It is never justified merely because a person refuses medicine. A decision requires a decision-specific assessment that the person lacks capacity, a recorded best-interests process, prescriber agreement and pharmacy advice confirming the proposed method will not alter the medicine unsafely.

The plan must name each medicine, method, review date and circumstances requiring reconsideration. Staff follow the current authorised plan exactly and record every administration on the MAR. If the person regains capacity, the covert plan cannot continue on the authority of an earlier assessment.

Returned or expired controlled drugs are stored in the designated segregated section until pharmacy collection. Destruction requires the authorised witness and a contemporaneous register entry.

## Preparation and interruption control

The administering worker prepares medicines for one person at a time and keeps the MAR available throughout the round. Medicines are not pre-poured for several people to save time. If preparation is interrupted before identity or medicine checks are complete, the worker returns to the beginning of the checking sequence.

The medicine trolley remains locked whenever the authorised worker is not in direct control of it. Keys are carried by the designated worker and are not left in a drawer, door or shared hiding place. Medicines taken away from the normal administration area remain labelled and under the worker's control until administered or returned to secure storage.

## Omissions, refusal and swallowing difficulty

When a person refuses a medicine, staff respect the decision, record the refusal using the correct MAR code and consider any immediate clinical risk. They do not disguise the medicine in food or drink unless the covert-administration process has been lawfully completed for that specific medicine.

A medicine is not recorded as administered until staff have reasonable evidence it was taken. If a tablet is dropped, spat out or later found, staff preserve what is safe to preserve, record the facts and seek advice before offering a replacement dose. Uncertainty is escalated; it is not resolved by guessing that the dose was or was not absorbed.

New swallowing difficulty triggers clinical review. Staff do not crush tablets, open capsules or mix medicines with food unless current medicine-specific advice authorises that route. A general statement that the person “prefers medicines crushed” is not sufficient.

## Time-critical and high-risk medicines

The care plan identifies time-critical medicines and the permitted administration window. Staff prioritise these medicines when a round is disrupted and seek clinical advice if the window is likely to be missed. The standard two-hour round does not silently redefine a narrower prescribed interval.
